title: GTA-RAG: Graph-Trajectory-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Turn Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning

visual_explainer.question: What behavior is supervised when graph paths are converted into retriever-validated search trajectories?
visual_explainer.takeaway: Graph paths define target evidence chains, retriever validation makes them executable, and trajectory reward trains search behavior before natural-QA reward.
visual_explainer.compared_with: The same model and retrieval package trained without trajectory-guided reward.

analysis.tldr: GTA-RAG uses graph-sampled, retriever-validated target chains as executable supervision before natural-question RL. A same-package ablation improves full-chain acquisition and QA, but the headline comparison bundles graph construction, hybrid retrieval, synthetic data, and two-stage optimization.
analysis.problem: Answer-only reward can succeed without teaching which sequence of searches should acquire a complete multi-hop evidence chain.
analysis.core_idea: Sample paths from an offline OpenIE graph, retain only targets reachable by the deployed retriever, turn them into search trajectories, and reward target-document acquisition before optimizing answer EM.
analysis.agent_loop: query → search hybrid graph+dense interface → inspect retrieved documents → continue until target chain is covered → answer
analysis.retrieval_design: Training targets are tied to a graph path and validated against the actual retriever. Inference uses a PPR+dense union interface; therefore the policy evidence is package-specific.
compared_to: same Qwen2.5-7B package without trajectory-guided reward
graph-RAG and search-RL systems under unmatched substrates
analysis.evidence: Full versus no trajectory reward gives EM/F1 49.7/59.4 versus 46.2/56.0 and full-chain coverage 74.1 versus 58.7. On held-out graph-synthetic questions, complete-chain coverage is 74.1 versus 54.3.
analysis.why_it_matters: It makes evidence-chain acquisition an explicit learning target rather than assuming answer reward will discover useful retrieval behavior.
limitations: Held-out trajectory questions come from the same graph-path construction used to define training targets.
The data are overwhelmingly two-hop, with only eight four-hop examples.
Headline baselines do not share graph construction, retrieval interface, synthetic generator, or full budget.
No complete graph-build, generator, online token, latency, memory, or dollar accounting is reported.
The repository's current three-stage script does not exactly match the paper's reported two-stage recipe.
